text: Loaded checkpoint:benchmarks/modadd/model/model.pt on local-full (full precision (local)).
H1 (behaviour): the model computes (a+b) mod 113 at the last position with near-perfect accuracy over the full 113x113 grid. Against: baseline accuracy near chance (~1/113).
dataset
baseline
E0002 (local-full): accuracy 1.0 on all 12769 pairs; mean logit diff 72.4 (clean) vs -72.5 (corrupt). H1 supported.

H2 (embedding structure): the token embedding W_E over integers 0..112 is sparse in the Fourier basis mod 113 — a handful of key frequencies carry most of the norm. Against: Fourier power spread roughly evenly across all 56 frequencies (no frequency with >>1/56 share).
periodicity

E0003 (local-full): W_E Fourier power is sparse. Top frequencies 28 (28.5%), 17 (23.1%), 2 (20.0%), 14 (7.2%); uniform share would be 1.8%. 9 key freqs hold 91.8% of power. Saved subspace A0001 (dim 18).

H3 (output structure): W_U (over output classes 0..112) is sparse in Fourier space, concentrated on the same main frequencies as W_E (28, 17, 2, 14). Against: W_U's top frequencies are different from W_E's, or W_U's power is spread out.
periodicity

E0004 (local-full): W_U uses the same top frequencies, 28 (30.0%), 17 (24.2%), 2 (21.6%), 14 (9.1%), then 27 and 43. 6 key freqs hold 90.1% of power. The input and output sides share one frequency set {2,14,17,28} (plus minor 27, 43).

H4 (where): the attention heads at position 2 move a and b information from positions 0/1 into the '=' position, and the MLP at position 2 does the nonlinear combination; all of these matter. Screen: attribution patching over heads/layers/positions. Against: the attention heads or the MLP have negligible attribution.
attribution_patching

E0005 (local-full, attribution estimate, n=512 seed 1): mlp_out at pos 2 = 0.99 normalised effect, attn_out at pos 2 = 0.59, the 4 heads are similar (0.14-0.17 each), resid at pos 0 and pos 1 = 0.28 each. Only pos 2 outputs matter (attn/mlp at pos 0,1 = 0). This fits H4 but is a first-order estimate; next I confirm with exact ablation.

H4a: mean-ablating each of the 4 heads on its own, and mlp0 on its own, hurts accuracy a lot; the heads share the work (no one head is enough). Against: some head can be ablated with accuracy staying ~1.0 (it is redundant), or ablating mlp0 leaves accuracy high.
ablation

E0006 (local-full, full grid, mean ablation): each head alone removes 28-34% of the logit diff (0.1: 72.4->47.9; 0.0: ->50.3; 0.2: ->51.2; 0.3: ->52.0). All 4 matter about equally, but none is needed on its own: the logit diff stays ~50, which is still a big margin. Revised: the heads share the work (each carries part of the frequency set?). Still to test: mlp0 alone, and all heads together.

H4b: mean-ablating mlp0 alone destroys the behaviour (logit diff near 0 or below, accuracy near chance), and so does jointly mean-ablating all 4 heads. Against: logit diff stays well above 0 after either ablation.
ablation
ablation

E0007: mean-ablating mlp0 drops the logit diff from 72.4 to 1.03 (1.4% of clean). E0008: jointly mean-ablating all 4 heads drops it to -0.07 (0%). Both the attention block and the MLP are necessary. H4b supported.

H5 (attention reads): from the '=' query (pos 2), every head splits its attention between pos 0 (a) and pos 1 (b), with little on pos 2 itself, so each head output holds a mix of the a and b embeddings. Against: some head puts >70% on '=' or attends to only one operand everywhere.
attention_patterns
How much attention goes from '=' to itself? (tests H5)

E0009/E0010 (local-full, n=1024 seed 2): from the '=' query, each head's mean attention to its most-attended operand is 0.500-0.503, and attention to '=' itself is only 0.0018-0.0021. So on average each head attends ~50/50 to a and b. The head outputs are a near-equal mix of the a and b token values, so the attention adds the two embedding signals together and does not do the arithmetic. Limitation: this is a mean; I did not measure how much the a/b split varies from example to example.

H6 (MLP reads): the MLP neuron activations at pos 2, seen as a function of the operand a (and of b), are periodic with the same key frequencies {2,14,17,28} found in W_E/W_U. Against: the key frequencies of the MLP activations differ from W_E's, or the power is spread out.
periodicity

E0011 (local-full, full grid): 510/512 neurons are active; on average 70% of a neuron's variance is on one frequency, and 199 neurons have >85% on one. Neurons cluster by frequency: k=2: 190, k=28: 128, k=17: 113, k=14: 52, k=27: 19 (a few at 43/56). This is the same frequency set as W_E/W_U (E0003, E0004). The MLP works in separate frequency channels.

H7 (the information used is only the key-frequency Fourier components): replacing the a and b embeddings with their mean, while keeping only their projection onto the 18-dim key-frequency subspace A0001, leaves performance near clean. Mean-ablating that subspace destroys it. Against: keeping the subspace alone gives <70% of the clean logit diff, or ablating it leaves >30%.
Ablate the key-frequency subspace of the embeddings at a and b
Ablate everything outside the key-frequency subspace (keep only A0001)

E0012 (local-full, full grid): mean-ablating the 18-dim key-frequency subspace A0001 of the a and b embeddings drops the logit diff from 72.4 to -0.085 (0%). The necessity half of H7 is supported. E0013 tried to keep only that subspace with "complement": true, but it returned exactly the same number (-0.085451). The flag was evidently ignored, so E0013 is NOT a valid sufficiency test. The sufficiency half of H7 stays open; I will test it in verify_hypothesis (circuit-alone check with the subspace).

Tooling gap: the ablation primitive does not support a complement/keep-only subspace option (E0013 duplicates E0012). I am not retrying with guessed flags. Sufficiency goes through verify_hypothesis, which does "ablate everything else" on its own.

H8 (who writes the answer): the correct-answer logit is written directly mostly by mlp0. The heads mainly feed the MLP (their direct logit contribution is small, <25% of the total). Against: heads' direct logit attribution is comparable to or bigger than mlp0's.
direct_logit_attribution

E0014 (local-full, full grid): the 4 heads write only 0.90 of the 72.4 logit diff directly (1.2%): 0.0=0.30, 0.1=0.25, 0.3=0.21, 0.2=0.15. The DLA tool reported heads only; the MLP number was not given. With E0007 (mlp0 ablation -> 1.03), the answer is written by mlp0 (plus whatever passes through the residual). Heads act through the MLP, not directly.

H9 (the MLP does the multiplication): before the MLP (resid_mid at pos 2), the residual is a sum of separate a and b features, so the answer class (a+b) mod 113 is NOT linearly decodable there. After the MLP (mlp_act / resid_post at pos 2) it is linearly decodable with high accuracy. Against: the held-out probe accuracy for (a+b) mod 113 on resid_mid is already high (>50%), or it is low after the MLP.

The linear_probe call for H9 failed (ValueError: the probe needs an explicit label list with one label per input; the string "answer" was read as 6 labels). Not counted as an experiment. H9 stays untested by probe; I'll try to get the same evidence from a 2-D Fourier look at the MLP output instead.

H10 (the MLP output is a function of a+b): the mlp_out vector at pos 2, over the full (a,b) grid, has its Fourier power on the key frequencies, and those components vary with (a+b) (the joint/diagonal terms), not with a or b alone. Against: mlp_out power sits mainly in a-only or b-only terms, or on frequencies outside the key set.
periodicity

E0015 (local-full, full grid): every one of the 128 mlp_out dims at pos 2 is periodic, with its best frequency in the key set: 28 (109 dims), 17 (14), 2 (5). On average 61% of a dim's variance is on one frequency. The MLP output is built from the key frequencies. The primitive only reports one best frequency per unit and does not split a-only / b-only / (a+b) terms, so the 'depends on a+b' half of H10 is NOT tested here. Revised to: mlp_out is built from key frequencies (supported); the a+b dependence is not shown by this experiment.

H11 (read-out goes through the key frequencies): mean-ablating the 12-dim W_U key-frequency subspace A0002 (freqs 2,14,17,27,28,43) in resid_post at pos 2 destroys the logit diff (<10% of clean). Against: >30% of the clean logit diff survives.
ablation

E0016 (local-full, full grid): mean-ablating the 12-dim W_U key-frequency subspace A0002 in resid_post at pos 2 drops the logit diff from 72.4 to 0.14 (0.2% of clean). The answer is read out entirely through the key-frequency directions. Caveat: A0002 was derived from W_U itself, so this mainly confirms that the logit-relevant part of the residual lives in those 12 dims (out of 128).

H12 (full algorithm): (1) W_E maps a and b to cos/sin features at key frequencies K={2,14,17,27,28,...} (E0003). (2) All 4 heads at '=' average the a and b token information ~50/50 (E0009, E0010), mixing them into one residual vector. (3) mlp0 neurons, each tuned to one frequency in K (E0011), combine the a and b features nonlinearly and write key-frequency directions (E0015). (4) W_U reads those directions at the same frequencies (E0004, E0016): logit(c) ~ sum_k alpha_k cos(w_k (a+b-c)), w_k=2*pi*k/113, which peaks at c=(a+b) mod 113. Verification test: on held-out seed 7, predict() matches the model ~100%; keeping only the key-frequency embedding subspace A0001 at a,b (everything else mean-ablated) keeps most of the logit diff; ablating that subspace breaks it; a random subspace of the same size does little. Against: circuit-alone retains <70%, or the random control breaks the behaviour about as much as the circuit.
Fourier frequency algorithm for (a+b) mod 113: verified. Passed at full precision.

V0001 (local-full, held-out seed 7, n=1000): VERIFIED. predict() agrees with the model on 1000/1000. Keeping only the 18-dim key-frequency embedding subspace at a,b (110 of 128 dims mean-ablated) keeps 99.8% of the logit diff with 100% accuracy; this closes the sufficiency gap left by E0013. Removing that subspace gives -0.1% and 0.9% accuracy (chance ~0.9%). Removing a random 18-dim subspace keeps 86.4% with 100% accuracy. Caveat: since the model is 100% accurate, any correct algorithm would score 100% agreement. Agreement does not on its own show the exact logit shape sum_k cos(w_k(a+b-c)). The mechanism claims rest on E0003/E0004/E0011/E0015/E0012/E0016.
